rules.title: Verified answers exist for the highest-frequency questions
rules.requirement: The most frequently asked and highest-consequence questions in the scope must be covered by verified answers rather than left to generation.
rules.rationale: A verified answer returns a curated visual instead of triggering DAX generation. It is the most direct fix for both latency and correctness on the questions that matter most, and it is the mechanism that stops repeated broad scans for the same recurring question.

check.how: Rank in-scope questions by frequency and consequence; confirm the top tier has verified answers.

rules.remediation: Build verified answers from existing report visuals for the top questions before tuning anything else.
rules.impactIfViolated: Every recurring question re-plans a query from scratch, at full token and scan cost, with non-deterministic results.

rules.title: Each verified answer carries five to seven trigger questions
rules.requirement: Every verified answer should define roughly five to seven trigger questions covering natural variations in phrasing, including both formal and conversational wording.
rules.rationale: Stated explicitly as five to seven trigger questions per verified answer. Too few and the answer never fires; the trigger set is what determines hit rate.

check.how: Count trigger questions per verified answer and review phrasing variety.

rules.remediation: Harvest real phrasings from usage logs and support requests rather than writing variations from imagination.
rules.impactIfViolated: Verified answers exist but rarely fire, so the tuning effort produces no measurable benefit.

rules.title: Verified answers use no more than three filters
rules.requirement: Configure up to three filters per verified answer to keep it flexible for slicing.
rules.rationale: Documented limit of three filters per verified answer.

check.how: Count configured filters per verified answer.

rules.remediation: Where more slicing is needed, create a second verified answer rather than overloading one.
rules.impactIfViolated: Configuration rejected or the answer becomes too narrow to fire.

rules.title: No verified answer references a hidden column
rules.requirement: Verified answers must not reference hidden columns or measures.
rules.rationale: Stated flatly: verified answers will not work if they reference hidden columns. The failure is silent, which makes it expensive to diagnose.

check.how: For each verified answer, resolve referenced objects and confirm none are hidden.

rules.remediation: Unhide the referenced object or rebuild the verified answer on a visible equivalent.
rules.impactIfViolated: Verified answers silently never fire and the team concludes the feature does not work.

rules.title: Verified answers are re-saved after any referenced object is renamed
rules.requirement: Renaming a table, column or measure referenced by a verified answer requires updating and re-saving that verified answer.
rules.rationale: Explicit rule. Renames are routine during model tuning, so this breaks constantly unless it is part of the change process.

check.how: Confirm the model change process includes a verified-answer revalidation step after renames.

rules.remediation: Add verified answer revalidation to the rename checklist and to the release pipeline.
rules.impactIfViolated: A cosmetic rename silently disables the curated answers protecting your top questions.

rules.title: Verified answer authoring prerequisites are met
rules.requirement: Authors creating verified answers in the Power BI service must be in a Copilot-enabled workspace, hold authoring permission on the underlying semantic model, be on a report page in edit mode, with the visual selected.
rules.rationale: All five conditions are documented prerequisites. When the option is greyed out, one of them is unmet - this list is the diagnostic.

check.how: Confirm the authoring team meets all five conditions and that the checklist is in the authoring guide.

rules.remediation: Publish the five conditions in the authoring guide as a troubleshooting checklist.
rules.impactIfViolated: Authors blocked with no visible reason and the capability goes unused.

rules.title: Verified answer coverage is measured against actual question volume
rules.requirement: The proportion of real user questions answered by a verified answer rather than by generation must be measured and tracked over time.
rules.rationale: Coverage is the leading indicator for both cost and consistency. It is also the only way to know whether verified-answer investment is paying back.

check.how: Sample real questions over a period and classify each as verified-answer hit or generated. Report the hit rate.

rules.remediation: Feed the miss list back into verified answer creation each cycle. The threshold here is a working target, not a Microsoft-published figure.
rules.impactIfViolated: No feedback loop; verified answers stay frozen at their initial guess of what users would ask.

rules.title: AI instructions exist and carry business context
rules.requirement: AI instructions must be configured with industry and business context, key terminology definitions, table and field mapping guidance, measure specifications and synonyms, and audience prioritization rules.
rules.rationale: These five content elements are the documented structure. AI instructions influence more Copilot capabilities than any other single configuration - report summary, questions about visuals, questions about the semantic model, create report page, and DAX query.

check.how: Review the AI instructions against the five required content elements.

rules.remediation: Structure the instructions on the documented template, then test with real questions.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator has no map from business vocabulary to model objects.

rules.title: AI instructions are configured in Prep for AI, not at data agent level, for semantic models
rules.requirement: For semantic model sources, AI instructions must be set in Prep for AI. Data agent level instructions are ignored for semantic model DAX generation.
rules.rationale: Stated as a direct rule. This is a high-frequency configuration mistake: teams write careful agent instructions for a semantic model source and none of it reaches the DAX generator.

check.how: For each semantic model source, confirm the substantive instructions live in Prep for AI and that agent-level instructions contain only cross-source guidance.

rules.remediation: Move semantic model guidance into Prep for AI; keep agent instructions for formatting, routing, abbreviations and tone across sources.
rules.impactIfViolated: Instructions written, paid for in tokens, and ignored by the generator.

rules.title: Instructions are focused and specific rather than long and complex
rules.requirement: AI instructions must be kept focused and specific; conflicting or overly complex instructions must be avoided.
rules.rationale: Documented on two counts: clear instructions are more effective than complex or conflicting ones, and overly complex instructions reduce accuracy while increasing latency. Instructions are also billed as input tokens on every single request, so verbosity has a direct and recurring CU cost.

check.how: Review instruction length and internal consistency; flag contradictory directives and unbounded lists.

rules.remediation: Cut instructions to the rules that changed behaviour in testing. Measure the token cost per request before and after.
rules.impactIfViolated: Higher latency, higher CU burn on every question, and lower accuracy.

rules.title: Instructions map user terminology to model objects
rules.requirement: Instructions must explicitly map the terms users say to the tables, measures and columns they mean, including synonyms and abbreviations.
rules.rationale: The documented example does exactly this: routing Clients, Customers and Organizations to the Accounts table, and Leads, Deals and Sales Prospects to the opportunities table. Terminology mapping is the highest-yield content in an instruction set.

check.how: Confirm the instructions contain explicit term-to-object mappings covering the main business vocabulary.

rules.remediation: Build the mapping from observed user language, not from the data dictionary.
rules.impactIfViolated: Correct questions in the users' own words routed to the wrong table.

rules.title: Instructions are treated as influence, not guarantee
rules.requirement: Governance documentation and user communication must state that the model interprets instructions but does not guarantee following them exactly.
rules.rationale: Stated directly. It sets the expectation that instructions reduce error rates rather than eliminate them, which is essential framing for any validity discussion.

check.how: Confirm the limitation is stated in the governance documentation and user-facing guidance.

rules.remediation: State it plainly and pair every critical instruction with a verified answer where correctness genuinely matters.
rules.impactIfViolated: Instructions treated as a control they are not, leaving critical answers unprotected.

rules.title: Data source instructions cover authoritative tables, joins, grain and default filters
rules.requirement: Each data source's instructions must state the authoritative tables per subject, the join keys and required join paths, the table grain and deduplication rules, the default filters such as current or active records only, date logic including fiscal calendars and time-zone assumptions, and any required calculations or output columns.
rules.rationale: This is the documented content list for data source instructions, and it is the most direct available control on generated query shape. Default filters in particular are what stops a query scanning full history when the user meant current records.

check.how: Review each source's instructions against the six documented content areas.

rules.remediation: Write the instructions from the documented list, and be specific about default filters and grain.
rules.impactIfViolated: The agent scans wide, joins wrong, double-counts on grain, and returns history when the user meant now.

rules.title: Example queries stay within 100 per data source and demonstrate reusable patterns
rules.requirement: Each data source may carry up to 100 example queries. Each should demonstrate one reusable pattern - multi-table joins or required preaggregation, business-specific calculations, relative dates and fiscal periods or snapshot logic, filters mapping user terminology to stored values, and ranking or window functions.
rules.rationale: 100 per data source is the documented cap, and the pattern list is the documented prioritization. Examples are few-shot grounding: they are the most efficient way to teach correct query shape.

check.how: Count example queries per source and review each for a single clear reusable pattern.

rules.remediation: Prioritize the five documented pattern categories. Keep each example focused on one pattern; fewer sharp examples beat many overlapping ones, and every example is billed as input tokens on each request.
rules.impactIfViolated: Query shapes are reinvented per question, inefficiently and inconsistently.

rules.title: The 25 row by 25 column response cap is designed for, not discovered
rules.requirement: Agent question scope and instructions must account for the maximum of 25 rows and 25 columns per response.
rules.rationale: Hard documented cap. An agent asked to list all customers will silently return a truncated view, and the user will not know it is truncated unless the design anticipated this.

check.how: Review the question scope for enumeration-style questions and confirm instructions direct the agent to aggregate or rank rather than list.

rules.remediation: Instruct the agent to aggregate, rank or top-N by default, and to state when results are truncated.
rules.impactIfViolated: Silently truncated answers presented as complete.

rules.title: Agent instructions are reserved for cross-source concerns
rules.requirement: Agent-level instructions must cover only cross-source guidance - formatting, source routing, abbreviations and tone - with source-specific logic held at the source or in Prep for AI.
rules.rationale: Documented scope for agent-level instructions. Mixing source-specific logic into agent instructions both fails to reach the semantic model generator and inflates the token cost of every request across all sources.

check.how: Review agent instructions for source-specific logic that belongs at source level.

rules.remediation: Relocate source-specific content and keep the agent layer thin.
rules.impactIfViolated: Instructions that are simultaneously ignored where needed and billed everywhere.

rules.title: Time filters are required for KQL and time-series sources
rules.requirement: For KQL and Eventhouse sources, agent instructions must direct the inclusion of time filters, and users must be guided to include a time range in their questions.
rules.rationale: Documented performance guidance for KQL time-series data. An unbounded time-series query is the purest form of the scan-everything behaviour.

check.how: Confirm KQL source instructions mandate a default time window, and that the default is stated.

rules.remediation: Set an explicit default such as the last 7 days unless the user states otherwise, and have the agent state the window it used.
rules.impactIfViolated: Full-retention scans on every time-series question, at severe latency and CU cost.

rules.title: Agent language scope is limited to English
rules.requirement: The rollout plan must record that non-English languages are not supported by Fabric data agents.
rules.rationale: Documented limitation. It determines which regions and business units can be in scope at all.

check.how: Confirm the rollout scope and user communication state the English-only constraint.

rules.remediation: Scope the audience accordingly and state it in the user guidance rather than letting users discover it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Non-English users receive poor answers and attribute it to model quality.

rules.title: Conversation history volatility is accounted for in user guidance
rules.requirement: User guidance must state that conversation history may not persist and can be reset by infrastructure changes, updates or model upgrades, and that a new chat session is recommended when follow-up answers drift.
rules.rationale: Documented behaviour on both counts: history may be lost, and because responses are automatically limited and summarized, follow-ups built on that limited context can go wrong.

check.how: Confirm the user guidance covers history volatility and the new-session recommendation.

rules.remediation: Add it to the user guidance and to the in-product tips where the surface allows.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users chase increasingly wrong answers down a degraded context chain.

rules.title: The underlying LLM cannot be changed - accept and design around it
rules.requirement: Design decisions must not assume the ability to substitute the model behind a Fabric data agent.
rules.rationale: Documented limitation. Where model behaviour is unacceptable, the levers are schema, instructions, examples and verified answers - not the model.

check.how: Confirm no architecture decision depends on model substitution.

rules.remediation: Direct tuning effort at the grounding configuration instead.
rules.impactIfViolated: Effort spent on an option that does not exist.

rules.title: Agents are split by subject area rather than consolidated
rules.requirement: Where the question scope spans several unrelated subject areas, separate narrowly scoped agents must be used instead of one agent bound to the maximum five sources.
rules.rationale: Follows directly from the documented guidance to select only relevant objects for the question scope in order to reduce ambiguity and latency. A single wide agent must route across every bound source on every question.

check.how: Review the subject-area breadth of each agent against its bound sources.
check.expected: agents scoped to coherent subject areas

rules.remediation: Split by subject area; accept more agents in exchange for narrower reasoning per question.
rules.impactIfViolated: Routing errors and latency scale with source count on every question.

rules.title: Schema object descriptions are used on the preview runtime where available
rules.requirement: Where the preview runtime supports schema object descriptions, they must be applied to abbreviated or generic names, columns with codes, flags, units or category values, date columns tied to a business event, and objects in large schemas.
rules.rationale: Documented as a preview-runtime capability with a specific priority list for where it matters.

check.how: Confirm the runtime version, then review description coverage across the priority categories.

rules.remediation: Apply descriptions following the documented priority order.
rules.impactIfViolated: Non-semantic-model sources reason from bare column names.
